# Follow-up: how widespread is receipt drift in the 25 Nov handoff?

**Record:** `research/records/2026-11-25-meta-science/` — follow-up to the confirmatory essay (`ARTICLE.md`,
`01f9e45`).
**Branch:** `research/meta-science-silent-failures-2026-11-25` · **Base:** `origin/main` @ `55732f4`
**Status: EXPLORATORY / POST-HOC.** The question was generated by the confirmatory essay's sixth finding (the
"eq03 TWFE transpose" receipt that does not exist). The documents were chosen after that finding, so the counts
below are a targeted audit of two documents, **not** a base rate. Protocol and status definitions were committed
first: `PRE_REGISTRATION_FOLLOWUP.md` @ `f474e23`. This report does not edit `ARTICLE.md` or `RECEIPTS.csv`.

---

## Answer in one paragraph

Receipt **existence** is clean in these two documents; receipt **content** is not. Of 46 audited assertions,
**38 VERIFIED, 5 COALESCED, 1 WRONG-COMMIT, 2 MISSING**. Every named branch exists and every named commit
resolves; 19/20 MIGRATION head claims were the branch tip at publication and 4/4 NEON fix-table heads were
correct. Drift sits in the layer between a receipt and what it is said to show: a **stale head** (one row
off by a single commit), a **wrong-object description** (`e.exits` vs `e.kids`), two **coalesced number/verdict
claims** in the DHS paragraph, a **local-only branch that lives in a different Git repository**, an
**item-number renumbering** between the two documents, and a **number whose per-cell receipt was never
committed**. That is the same shape as the eq03 case — a correct object inheriting a claim it no longer
supports — and it is concentrated, not pervasive.

## Method (summary; full protocol in `PRE_REGISTRATION_FOLLOWUP.md`)

Documents pinned to commits and time-indexed to their committer times:
`MIGRATION_2026-11-25.md` @ `354f7c0` (00:17:31 +08) and `NEON_FREE_FIXES_2026-11-25.md` @ `6f68776`
(00:46:47 +08). For each claim: resolve branch/commit (`git rev-parse`, `git cat-file -t`), test reachability
(`git merge-base --is-ancestor`), inspect content (`git show --stat`, `git show <sha> -- <path>`,
`git show <sha>:<path>`), and recompute numbers where the receipt contains data (JSON counts, sha256 manifests).
Head claims use a **time-indexed rule**: walk the branch's first-parent chain and take the newest commit whose
committer time is ≤ the document's committer time; a claimed SHA that is older than that is a stale head.
Host-only git reads; no server, no power actions.

Status definitions: **VERIFIED** (receipt exists, content matches, head rule passes); **COALESCED** (receipts
exist but the claim merges ≥2 objects/versions/fixes/numbers); **WRONG-COMMIT** (receipt exists but the claim's
content is not in it, or the head was stale at publication); **MISSING** (no receipt in the audited repository).
One row per audited assertion; evidence with paths/lines in `results/receipt_audit.csv`.

### What verifies cleanly (do not lose this result)

- **All 20 MIGRATION branches exist** and all 20 claimed heads are ancestors of their origin refs; 19 were the
  exact tip at publication (the 20th is finding F1). Six branches have moved since (expected; not drift).
- **All four NEON fix rows verify**: the head was the tip at publication in 4/4; the diffs contain the named fixes;
  the named tests exist. Host-side re-runs from the cited commits: `test_guards.py` @ `22c4bb8` → **ALL PASS**;
  `test_exit_reason.py` @ `219747a` → **ALL PASS**; `test_bench_guards.py` @ `2c575d9` → **ALL PASS**;
  the committed test-bench data manifest re-hashes **4/4 OK**.
- **Papers line:** `a22f3c4`, `5a56864`, `2bcb7d7` all exist and are the heads of paper branches.
- The MIGRATION quarantine objects exist at the claimed heads: `estimate.py` with the `in samp` bug (`fe762b9`),
  `ir_pipeline.py` with v190/CMC/survey_type/PSU references (`f4a7f65`), `test_full_system.py` with `pinv`/`all([])`
  (`aadbbb4`), the six equation scripts (`a7fcfb9`), the test-bench F9 n=0 and `LinAlgError` report (`ab8ca9d`),
  and the gate-jobs `_record`/`spend_feedback` objects (`6728494`).

## Findings — drift beyond eq03 (C3)

**F1 — WRONG-COMMIT: a stale head in the MIGRATION status table.** The row `research/equation-test-bench-2026-11-25
| ab8ca9d` was one commit behind at publication: `02d930c` ("Session-retirement record…") has committer time
00:17:25, six seconds **before** the handoff commit at 00:17:31, and is `ab8ca9d`'s child. Anyone who checked out
the claimed head got a tree without the diagnostics commit. (Row `M-A1.10`; evidence:
`git rev-list --first-parent --timestamp origin/research/equation-test-bench-2026-11-25`.)

**F2 — COALESCED: the driver "reads `e.exits` incorrectly".** MIGRATION item 2 names the right file but the wrong
object: at the claimed head `b7108da` the driver does `k = e.kids`
(`run_edsystem_multiverse.py:114`), and `e.kids` has been compacted by `core.step`
(`keep = k['reason'] < 0`, `engine/eduengine/core.py`:446–447). The archive is `e.exits`; the read was the live
roster. The later correction (`4679ddb`, erratum `3afac25`) says "driver read e.kids", which is the code fact.
This is the same wrong-object shape as the exit bug itself, now in the handoff prose. (Rows `M-A3.2`.)

**F3 — COALESCED: "Point estimates unchanged."** In the same bullet that reports the D4 wanted-vs-actual
point estimate moving from −0.0775 to −0.1962, the NEON document says point estimates are unchanged. That sentence
merges (a) the cluster-bootstrap multiplicity fix (which changes only the resampling distribution) with (b) the
full construct×schooling interaction-set change (which moves the D4 point estimate). The record's own separation
commit lands **after** the NEON document: `9e063bf`, "separate the bootstrap CI change from the D4 interaction-set
change", 00:50:22 vs the document's 00:46:47. The document inherited the pre-separation attribution, which is the
exact conflation the confirmatory essay's case 1 documents. (Row `N-B3.1b`.)

**F4 — COALESCED: "now includes 1.0".** The DHS bullet presents one interval as the corrected run's. The
committed run contains two implementations: `corrected_results.json` @ `3faeff3` gives
`[0.9987338159871081, 1.1403490938072522]` (includes 1.0), while `results/africa11/results.json` and
`run.log:365` give `[1.001130354334825, 1.1402983948192367]` (excludes 1.0). The verdict flip is real for one
implementation and not the other; the document does not carry that qualifier. (Row `N-B3.1c`; this is the
discrepancy the confirmatory record reports unreconciled.)

**F5 — MISSING: a "local only" receipt that is not in this repository.** `Not pushed, local only:
fix/equation-suite-2026-11-25 (in ~/neon-boot/wt/eq)`. No such ref exists in the atlas repo. The cited path does
exist, but its `.git` file points at `/Users/treymenefee/massification_live/.git/worktrees/eq` — a worktree of a
**different Git repository**, not listed by `git worktree list` here. Per the no-touch rule for
`~/massification_live`, that repository was not inspected. The claim is explicitly local-only, so absence from
origin is expected; what is absent is any receipt a reader of *this* repository can check. (Row `N-B2.1a`.)

**F6 — COALESCED: quarantine items are renumbered between the two documents.** MIGRATION item 4 is the
equation-suite; item 5 is the test bench. The NEON fix table's row `#4` fixes the **test bench**, and its "Still
open" list starts `5. **equation-suite**`. So "Neon item 5" means test bench in one document and equation-suite in
the other, and "four items fixed" is a positional count, not the quarantine IDs. This is precisely the class of
reference drift that turned the eq03/eq09 bundle into an eq03 citation. (Row `N-B4.1b`.)

**F7 — MISSING: `21/49 supported rows fail cell-level sign checks` has no committed per-cell receipt.** The
49-row `full_system_tests.json` @ `aadbbb4` carries no per-cell counts (keys: `outcome, effect, se, p, ci,
stratum_min/max, sign_consistent, n, p_holm, supported`), so the number cannot be reproduced from the receipt.
The corrected record @ `22c4bb8` reports **17/45** supported rows with ≥1 cell sign flip and **6/45** with a
≥10 % flip (computed from `cell_sign_flips` / `cell_sign_flips_10pct`); different denominator and stricter
disclosure, so 21/49 is not necessarily wrong — it is unverifiable. (Row `M-A3.3b`.)

## Numeric reconciliations that are *not* drift (reported for completeness)

- MIGRATION item 1's predicted Africa-11 interval `[0.9987, 1.1323]` and full-sample `[0.9084, 1.0164]` are
  predictions ("should include 1.0"); the committed corrected values are `[0.9987, 1.1403]` and `[0.906, 1.019]`.
  Difference is Monte-Carlo noise, and the prediction is labelled as such.
- NEON's `-0.1962` was predicted by the handoff's quarantine note and reproduced; the confirmatory record
  documents this.
- NEON row 1's head (`3faeff3`) was the tip at publication, but the next commit (`45b974e`, provenance record)
  landed **9 seconds later** at 00:46:56. Time-indexed tie noted; not counted as drift.
- NEON row 2's head (`4679ddb`) is the **report-retraction** commit; the code fix and test are in its parent
  `219747a`. The table's branch-level claim is true; a reader who inspects only the head commit's diff sees the
  report change, not the code. Not counted as drift, but worth knowing (recorded in the row's evidence).
- NEON row 3's branch was later corrected (`3ddd190` 01:02, `3e35ff0` 01:16: "false-positive count is 4 rows
  total (49→45), not five"). Those are post-publication corrections of the same counts, not evidence that the
  head claim was wrong at 00:46:47.

## Limitations

- **Post-hoc and targeted.** The documents were selected because of the eq03 finding; the drift rate here cannot
  be generalised to the repository, to other handoffs, or to other authors.
- **Two documents only.** `HANDOFF.md`/`HANDOFF.txt`, per-branch records, and the "What is trustworthy" section
  were out of scope by pre-registration.
- **Time index has clock ties.** Head claims are judged by committer timestamps; the two near-ties (6 s for F1,
  9 s for the NEON row 1 note) are reported as seconds, not adjudicated.
- **Object-existence-only rows.** For quarantine items 1b (`ir_pipeline.py` blockers) and 6 (gate-jobs defects)
  the named objects were verified to exist but the defect semantics were not re-derived in this cheap audit.
  They are marked VERIFIED with that scope stated in the CSV evidence; they should not be cited as proof the
  defects are real.
- **Different repository not inspected.** The local-only branch pointer (F5) is reported at the pointer level
  only, per the no-touch rule.
- Commit timestamps are the author's environment's local (+08:00) values read from git; no attempt was made to
  correct for clock drift across agents.

All 46 rows are in `results/receipt_audit.csv` with the exact file/line evidence.

## Bottom line for the programme

The eq03 case was not a one-off: **8 of 46 audited assertions (17 %) drift**, in four distinct ways
(5 COALESCED, 1 WRONG-COMMIT, 2 MISSING). But the damage is in the *claims layer*, not the git layer — branches,
commits, paper SHAs, fix branches and named tests all resolve. The cheap, repeatable countermeasure is the one
this audit used: pin the document, pin the time, resolve the receipt, and check the claimed object **is the object
the receipt shows**. That is exactly `GUARDS_CHECKLIST.md` item 8 applied to prose.
